note: Fits the commercial half of the stated ICP cleanly: a New York City real estate broker with $100,000 months, plainly not deconditioned at 6'1", 182 lb and 16.7% body fat, training one to two hours a day and running three to five times a week, and framing the goal as refinement rather than rescue — 'I'm not overweight. I'm not like needing to lose weight for health reasons. It's more just like, I know I can do and be better.' Income is scored as a match because the constraint he described is lumpiness, not shortfall, and he offered to pay in full if it saved money. Where he falls outside is neglected_health: the ICP wants health to be the deprioritised area, not the emergency, and this prospect was hospitalised and paralysed for three days eight months ago with no diagnosis, remains under a neurologist, carries a testosterone of 272 and is four months into an unsuccessful GLP-1 course. That is a health crisis with a good income attached. This is the second time in the corpus that the observation already recorded in icp.json holds — the stated ICP has no clinical criterion, and here the missing criterion did not lose the deal, it sold one it arguably should have paused.
